title: BBQ Chicken Sliders
shortDescription: Sweet-smoky sliders for a hungry line
subtitle: Sweet-smoky sliders for a hungry line
description: Thighs simmered right in doctored BBQ sauce until they shred, piled on butter-toasted Hawaiian rolls with vinegar slaw and pickles. The braising liquid becomes the sauce, so nothing gets poured down the drain.
equipment: Dutch oven or wide heavy pot with lid
Two forks or a stand mixer with paddle for shredding
Griddle or sheet trays for toasting rolls

steps.title: Season the thighs while the pot heats
steps.instruction: Pat the chicken thighs dry and season all over with the smoked paprika, garlic powder, and kosher salt — seasoning the meat itself, not just the sauce, is why the shred tastes like BBQ all the way through instead of sauce-coated plain meat. Set the heavy pot over medium heat while you work.

steps.title: Simmer the thighs in sauce until they shred
steps.instruction: Nestle the thighs into the pot with 2 cups of the BBQ sauce and the chicken broth, cover, and hold a gentle simmer — small lazy bubbles, never a hard boil, which seizes the meat tight. Cook 25–30 minutes: the thighs pass the safe 165°F mark early, but keep going until an instant-read thermometer shows about 190°F, where the connective tissue melts and a fork twists through with no resistance.

steps.title: Shred the meat while it's hot
steps.instruction: Lift the thighs to a sheet tray with the slotted spoon and pull them apart with two forks into rough, bite-size shreds — or drop them in the stand mixer with the paddle for 20 seconds on low. Shred while hot; the meat lets go easily now and drinks sauce back up, where cooled meat fights the forks and stays dry.

steps.title: Reduce the pot liquid into the real sauce
steps.instruction: Turn the pot to medium-high and let the braising liquid bubble hard 5–8 minutes with the last cup of BBQ sauce, the apple cider vinegar, and the brown sugar, until it coats a spoon and a swipe across the back holds a line. The vinegar cuts the sweetness so the third slider tastes as good as the first. Fold the shredded meat back in and drop the heat to its lowest setting.

steps.title: Toss the vinegar slaw and chill it
steps.instruction: In the big bowl, toss the coleslaw mix with the mayonnaise, a splash of cider vinegar, and a pinch of salt until every shred is coated but not soupy. Park it in the fridge until build time — at least 10 minutes takes the raw edge off the cabbage, and cold crunchy slaw against hot meat is the whole point of this sandwich.

steps.title: Butter and toast the rolls
steps.instruction: Split the slider rolls, keeping each 12-pack sheet connected — they toast and move as one piece. Brush the cut faces with melted butter and toast on the griddle or under a 400°F oven for 3–4 minutes until golden at the edges. That toasted face is a moisture barrier; skip it and the first saucy scoop soaks the bread into mush.

steps.title: Build the sliders bottom-up
steps.instruction: Lift the meat with the slotted spoon so excess sauce drains back into the pot — the number-one slider mistake is drowning the bun. Layer each roll with a solid pinch of meat, two dill pickle chips, and a small mound of slaw, then cap it. Work in full sheets of 12 on trays; it goes five times faster than one sandwich at a time.

steps.title: Send trays out while the buns are crisp
steps.instruction: Serve within 10 minutes of building — these have about a 20-minute window before the slaw wilts warm and the bottom bun gives up. Keep the pot of extra meat on the lowest heat with a lid so the second and third rounds go out just as hot as the first tray did.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover the pulled chicken — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. Keep the vinegar slaw in the fridge, not on the counter — it's already dressed and needs to stay cold and crisp, not sit next to a warm pan. On return, spot-check the chicken at a safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool pulled chicken and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Thighs, not breasts — breast meat shreds into dry strings in a braise; thighs stay juicy through the simmer, the hold, and the reheat.
Take the meat well past 165°F to about 190°F before shredding — that's where thigh collagen turns to gelatin and the forks glide.
If the pot sauce tastes flat at the end, it wants another splash of cider vinegar before it wants more sugar or salt.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Log hold times on the pan with a grease pencil when tones drop mid-service.
Spot-check proteins with an instant-read thermometer before reopening the line after a call.
tonightSpread: Main: BBQ pulled chicken sliders on toasted Hawaiian rolls
Sides: vinegar slaw, dill pickle chips, kettle chips if the pantry has them
Condiments: extra warmed BBQ sauce for the double-dippers
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool pulled chicken in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Never store built sliders — keep meat, slaw, and rolls separate and the second shift eats as well as the first.
Reheat the meat in a covered pan with a splash of broth or water; day-two sauce thickens and scorches fast over bare heat.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Three-bite sandwiches with hot saucy meat, cold crunchy slaw, and a buttered crisp bun — a tray of 24 disappears before the second sheet finishes toasting.
substitutions: Rotisserie shortcut: fold 2.5 lb pulled rotisserie meat into the reduced sauce and skip the simmer — dinner lands in 25 minutes.
Regular burger buns work if slider rolls are gone — makes 8 full-size sandwiches; toast them the same way.
Greek yogurt swaps 1:1 for the mayonnaise in the slaw — tangier, lighter, and nobody has ever noticed.
No cider vinegar? White vinegar plus an extra pinch of brown sugar lands close enough.
